clue.text: End letters in support of bar

blocks.note: the goal is the end a team attacks, or an end aimed at
letters arrive in the post

explanation.surface: A sign-writer's last letters are fixed to a frame holding up a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End letters' looks like the last letters of words, but it is two separate words: an end and the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football or rugby pitch the upright posts hold up the crossbar between them.

clue.text: Work-to-rule neither starting nor finishing in the capital

indicators.note: with no start and no finish, the phrase loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: a go-slow is industrial action much like working to rule

explanation.surface: Strikers in a capital city are staging a work-to-rule that never quite begins or ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the outer letters of GO-SLOW leaves OSLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway; the clue leaves the country unnamed.

clue.text: One slow to grasp less than sparkling humour

blocks.note: dim light is less than sparkling
wit is clever humour

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't get jokes is given a rather flat sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is a stupid person, someone who takes a long time to understand things.

clue.text: Tea and fresh pitta bread

indicators.note: fresh means newly made, so the pitta is remade into a new order

blocks.note: cha is an informal word for tea
the word pitta rearranged

explanation.surface: A café order of a cuppa with some warm pitta.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is an unleavened flat Indian bread cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Prig left out what  shouldn't be worshipped on religious visit

indicators.note: out here means disordered or put out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
the commandment forbids worshipping a graven image

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious prig on a church trip sneers at idols the others ought not to adore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as omitted, but left is just L and 'out' scrambles it with PRIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey made to a holy place for devotional reasons.

clue.text: Game played with ale pot

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are moved about freely into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pub game played with a beer tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a Basque ball game played against a wall, the family of sports including jai alai.

clue.text: Proudly furnished with a snakebite, or something similar

blocks.note: the snake half of the word: a boa is a constricting snake
a sting is a bite from an insect

explanation.surface: Someone is proud to have been given a snakebite, or a similar wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snakebite' splits into snake and bite; 'or something similar' admits that a sting is not quite a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that boasts a pool has one and shows it off, so boasting means proudly possessing.

clue.text: Told to give Shed a pasting for being miserable?

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the phrase is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: Shed is the setter, so pasting him is a request to stick me down

explanation.surface: Someone is told to beat up the setter Shed because he is so dreary.
explanation.walkthrough: A pasting is a beating in the surface, but here it means applying paste: the setter asks to be glued.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy describes a person who is depressed, dejected and low in spirits.

clue.text: Next in line to adopt iron cow

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside the other

blocks.note: an heir is next in line to inherit
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: An heir to a farm takes on a cast-iron cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young female cow, one that has not yet had a calf.

clue.text: A band from the capital to boot

blocks.note: taken as written
the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A group of musicians from London is mentioned as an extra.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'band' is an orchestra rather than a rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning as well or in addition, which is what also means.

clue.text: Court resolution on gang leader given "time" or "bird"

indicators.note: the leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of gang is kept

blocks.note: to court someone is to woo them
dots per inch, the measure of a printer's or screen's resolution
the opening letter of the word
an eon is an immensely long period of time

explanation.surface: A court rules on a gang boss who is handed time, or a stretch inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' and 'bird' both look like slang for a prison sentence; time is EON and the bird is the real definition. DPI is dots per inch.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood pigeon is a large grey pigeon, common in European woods and farmland.

clue.text: Sturdy black roustabout

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word before it wraps round the colour letter

blocks.note: the word read as roust followed by about
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A strong dark-skinned oil-rig labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: Roustabout, a labourer, splits into roust plus about.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and healthy, able to withstand hard use, just as sturdy does.

clue.text: Not much happening in patchy Berlin airlift?

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting a word turns it upwards, so it is read bottom to top

blocks.note: patchy work is uneven
Berlin air is the German word for air, with lift as the instruction

explanation.surface: A quiet spell during the 1948 Berlin airlift, when supplies were flown in irregularly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Berlin airlift is a real event, but 'Berlin air' means the German word, and 'lift' raises it.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneventful period is one where little or nothing of note takes place.

clue.text: Compiler's largely unintelligent and less than absolutely fabulous

indicators.note: largely means mostly, so not the whole word: its last letter goes
less than the full word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the compiler speaking of himself
thick means stupid
all in the sense of completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being rather dim and only partly Absolutely Fabulous.
explanation.walkthrough: Absolutely Fabulous is a British TV sitcom, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its root sense means belonging to fable, so legendary and imaginary like mythical.

clue.text: Initiate a set, having the support beforehand

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone starts a tennis set, having had support first.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby cutting its first teeth is starting off its set of teeth.

clue.text: It recedes with a crack of sorts

blocks.note: first meaning: the edge of the hair on the forehead, which moves back with age
second meaning: a very thin fracture, as in a bone or a cup

explanation.surface: Something withdraws as a fissure opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A balding man has a receding hairline, and a hairline crack or fracture is a very fine one.

clue.text: Heart of pilot dying to do for his ruler?

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so only the central letters are kept and the ends go

blocks.note: a pilot who dies by crashing his plane into the target
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suicide pilot of the Second World War is keen to die for his emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Kamikaze pilots dived to their deaths for the Japanese emperor, so the whole clue describes them; the middle four letters of the pilot are MIKA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado was the title used in the West for the Emperor of Japan, the kamikaze pilot's sovereign.

clue.text: Member rings round first for object of introvert's attention

blocks.note: a round letter
Member of Parliament
haloes are rings of light

explanation.surface: A body part is encircled by rings, which an introvert stares at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' tempts a reading as a body part; it is the parliamentary kind. Navel-gazing is the cliché of self-absorption.
explanation.definitionFit: Omphalos is Greek for navel, and contemplating one's navel is the classic image of inward-looking self-absorption.

clue.text: Breaks the gardener's tool

blocks.note: first meaning: snaps off under strain, as a bolt does
second meaning: large scissors for trimming hedges

explanation.surface: Someone smashes the gardener's equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt that shears snaps under sideways force, and garden shears are big two-bladed cutters.

clue.text: Active teacher returned to hospital feeling off-colour

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: a live wire is active
pupils address a male teacher as sir
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A busy teacher has gone back to hospital because he is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish describes someone feeling slightly sick or irritable, once blamed on a disordered liver.

clue.text: Burst in and sound pleased getting back into it

indicators.note: getting back suggests going in the opposite direction, so the word runs backwards
into places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a cat purrs when it is pleased

explanation.surface: Someone bursts in, purring with pleasure as they get back into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to enter forcibly or suddenly, rushing in like an invading force.

clue.text: Dwarf employing cunning to conceal backslash?

indicators.note: back means the following word is read in the opposite direction
concealing something hides it inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: sly means crafty
read as back plus slash, British slang for urinating

explanation.surface: A little person uses cunning to hide a keyboard character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backslash' is a single computer symbol in the surface, but splits into back plus slash, which is slang for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White.

clue.text: Time to enter the country part of Austria

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a country in the Middle East
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is time to cross into the country, a region of Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Styria is a federal state in south-east Austria, with Graz as its capital.

clue.text: Practise agriculture in religious community and produce flower

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: a friary houses a community of friars
to till is to cultivate the soil

explanation.surface: Monks farm their land and grow a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The fritillary is a bulb plant with chequered bell-shaped blooms, also the name of a butterfly.

clue.text: Kid's carriage representing Pythagoras's first memory

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the name

blocks.note: the opening letter of the mathematician's name
random-access memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A child's carriage stands for the mathematician's earliest recollection.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is a pushchair-like carriage in which a baby is wheeled about.

clue.text: Press for dismissal

blocks.note: first meaning: to apply force, or urge
second meaning: getting the sack

explanation.surface: Someone lobbies to have a person sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To push is to exert pressure, and being given the push is British slang for being fired.

clue.text: Volte-face about parking is a change for the better

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turn wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: a complete reversal of direction or opinion
P is the road-sign letter for parking

explanation.surface: A politician's sudden reversal on parking policy is welcomed as an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an improvement or rise, especially in economic fortunes.

clue.text: Careless mistakes by the carrier

blocks.note: slips are small errors
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A delivery firm is blamed for sloppy errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is done without care, sloppy and slapdash.
